source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Spotted/banded cucumber beetle and corn rootworm (ខ្ជុងខ្ជៅអុចលឿង, Diabrotica balteata, Diabrotica spp; Order Coleoptera, Family Chrysomelidae): this beetle is a small round-bodied insect, greenish in color with yellow spots/bands on the wing covers. It is roughly 2 mm in body length, up to about 1 cm. This insect burrows and lives in the soil, appearing after the soil surface is disturbed and looking similar to a small beetle with a pale gray-black coloring; both adults and larvae can be found feeding at the same time, roughly 6-9 mm long.

This pest lives underground and can persist in the soil for up to about 10 months, or 1 year, and can produce up to 2 generations per year. Adults feed on the corn silk during the flowering stage, weakening pollination when abundant on the silk.
